newsitem.title: USA: WHX to resume talks with steelworkers.
newsitem.headline: WHX to resume talks with steelworkers.

text.p: WHX Corp and the United Steelworkers union will resume contract talks on Wednesday, the company said.
"The full negotiating teams will meet...we're hoping this will be the beginning of talks that will lead to a resolution," said John Wiater, communications consultant for WHX.
Union officials were not available for comment. Some 4,500 steelworkers have been on strike at WHX since October 1.
The strike has idled eight steel plants in three states. WHX said recently it will post a loss in the fourth quarter as a result of the work stoppage.

The talks are scheduled to take place at a hotel in downtown Pittsburgh under the supervision of a federal mediator. It will mark the first time the two full negotiating teams have met since the strike began.
The chief negotiators for each side met in December but talks collapsed after one day.
Pensions remain the most contentious issue. The union wants WHX to establish a defined benefit plan, the type of plan covering union workers at other major steelmakers.
The company has maintained it cannot afford a defined benefit plan and instead offered to enhance its current defined contribution plan.
Wiater said both sides have stood firm on their positions. "It's been status quo since the strike began," he said.
